newsitem.title: JAPAN: US politician due in N.Korea for talks on detainee.
newsitem.headline: US politician due in N.Korea for talks on detainee.

text.p: U.S. Congressman Bill Richardson was due to fly to North Korea on Monday in the hope of bringing back American detainee Carl Hunziker, a U.S. State Department official in Tokyo said.

Richardson, a Democrat from New Mexico, was to act as an unofficial U.S. envoy in negotiations with North Korean officials. He was to leave Tokyo for Pyongyang on Monday afternoon, a U.S. official said.

Japan's Kyodo news agency reported that Richardson would be aiming to secure Hunziker's immediate release in exchange for a sum of money. Hunziker's family have agreed to pay $5,000 for his release, the agency said.
Kyodo said North Korea had demanded $100,000 for Hunziker's release, but the United States had rejected the demand on the grounds that the amount was too high.
Hunziker, 26, was arrested on August 24 after crossing the Yalu River from China into North Korea and accused of being a U.S. spy. Hunziker's family has denied the charge, saying he is a missionary.

U.S. State Department officials described Richardson's visit as "an important humanitarian mission", although he would be accompanied by a U.S. State Department official acting as an "escort officer".
Richardson has acted as Washington's troubleshooter on several previous missions to countries with which the United States has no formal diplomatic ties, including North Korea.
In December 1994, Richardson went to North Korea to negotiate the release of a U.S. pilot whose helicopter was brought down in North Korean airspace.
He had planned to visit North Korea in September but the trip was called off after an intrusion by a North Korean submarine into South Korean waters sparked a major crisis between the two Koreas.
